pages.title: File:Music and Words presents- Ádám Fellegi – Beethoven’s Three Faces.jpg

ObjectName.value: Music and Words presents- Ádám Fellegi – Beethoven’s Three Faces

Categories.value: Haus der Musik (Vienna)|Male pianists from Hungary|Files with coordinates missing SDC location of creation|Flickr images reviewed by FlickreviewR 2|Euphoria – Anatomy of Presence

ImageDescription.value:
Hungarian concert pianist and Franz Liszt Prize laureate Ádám Fellegi, photographed on 24 September 2026 during his performance at Haus der Musik in Vienna, Austria.

The interactive concert, entitled “The Three Stages of a Man's Life – Beethoven: The Lover, the Hero and the Sage”, explored three defining periods of Ludwig van Beethoven's life and artistic development: the passionate and expressive works of his youth, the heroic character of his middle period, and the profound musical reflections of his later years.

Combining live piano performance with personal reflections, historical context, musical explanations and direct interaction with the audience, the evening offered an interpretation of Beethoven's music and creative evolution. The event was presented by Music and Words.

The photograph forms work no. 03 of “EUFÓRIA – The Anatomy of Presence”, an ongoing photographic art project by Hungarian visual artist and photographer Norbert Bánhalmi. The series explores moments of authentic human presence captured in real-life situations, with particular attention to gestures, expressions, emotional intensity and the relationship between individuals and their surroundings.

Beyond its documentary significance, the photograph is intended to function as an independent work of photographic art within the EUFÓRIA series, connecting the historical and musical context of the performance with the artist's exploration of human presence.

The photographic documentation of the concert and the inclusion of the image in the EUFÓRIA series do not imply that Ádám Fellegi commissioned, sponsored or officially endorsed the photographic project.
